title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: Rough audience tape with severe crowd noise, but the performance shines on Good Lovin', Lovelight and a wild Hard‑to‑Handle/China‑Rider run.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience (crowd) tape that many listeners describe as muffled, noisy and almost unlistenable except for occasional flashes of clarity on tracks like "Lovelight".  Musically the show has its moments – fans rave about the jammed Good Lovin', a soaring Lovelight, and a surprising Hard‑to‑Handle into China/Rider sequence – making it an interesting historic document despite the poor sound quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Show receives praise for several jams, but recording is consistently called terrible; weighted average (70% show ≈4, 30% recording ≈2) yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very rough crowd tape with heavy din of drunken audience; many reviewers say you can barely hear the band, though brief moments (Lovelight) cut through. No soundboard source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Free concert with an acoustic opening by Garcia & Weir, a New Riders set, then the Dead.  The outdoor hill setting created a laid‑back vibe; despite sparse attendance the performance includes several memorable jams.
